name: Bristled Moorbounder
publication: Critical Role: Call of the Netherdeep
otherStatistics: Natural armor. Darkvision 60 ft. Passive Perception 11. No languages.
appearance: A muscular, tusked hunter with rows of long blade-shaped bristles along its back and sides.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast and Critical Role, Critical Role: Call of the Netherdeep, first printing, March 2022, Appendix A, Creatures, Moorbounders, p. 203. https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/cotn/creatures#Moorbounders
sections.Traits:
Bladed Hide. At the start of the moorbounder’s turn, each creature that is grappling it takes 5 (2d4) piercing damage.
Standing Leap. The moorbounder can long jump up to 40 ft. or high jump up to 20 ft. from a standstill or after a run.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Blades attack and one Claw attack.
Blades. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, 5 ft. reach, one target. A hit deals 11 (2d6 + 4) slashing damage.
Claw. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, 5 ft. reach, one target. A hit deals 14 (4d4 + 4) slashing damage.
sections.Encounter ecology: The bristled offshoot hunts in the marshes and muddy foothills of Xhorhas. Its sharp hide makes it a poor mount.
sections.Encounter application: In Moorbounder Mayhem on p. 43, two bristled moorbounders threaten a mounted scout. A character can spend an action to frighten one away with a successful DC 21 Charisma (Intimidation) check.
sections.Source notes: The adventure prints a standalone Beast block on p. 203. The attack is Claw in this printing.

name: Moonshark
publication: Critical Role: Call of the Netherdeep
otherStatistics: Natural armor. Perception +3. Blindsight 60 ft. Passive Perception 13. No languages.
appearance: A massive slate-gray shark with a silver spear lodged in its side. A thick rope holds a gold-and-emerald amulet to its body.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast and Critical Role, Critical Role: Call of the Netherdeep, first printing, March 2022, Chapter 1, A Fateful Competition, E10 Moonshark Lair, p. 33. Use the Giant Shark base block in the 2014 Monster Manual, p. 328. https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/cotn/a-fateful-competition#TheEmeraldGrotto
sections.Traits:
Blood Frenzy. The shark has advantage on melee attack rolls against creatures below their hit point maximum.
Water Breathing. The shark breathes only underwater.
Silver Spear. While the spear is lodged in its side, the shark sheds bright silver light within 10 ft. and dim light for another 10 ft. A character within 5 ft. can use an action to dislodge the spear with a successful DC 13 Strength (Athletics) check.
sections.Actions: Bite. Melee weapon attack, +9 to hit, 5 ft. reach, one target. A hit deals 22 (3d10 + 6) piercing damage.
sections.Bonus actions: Spear-assisted swim. While the spear is embedded, if the shark uses its action to Bite and misses, it can spend a bonus action to swim up to 25 ft. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks.
sections.Emerald Eye: The rope holding the amulet has AC 17 and 5 HP, and characters can attack it to cut the amulet free. If the shark is dead or incapacitated, a character can remove the rope as an action.
sections.Encounter ecology: The Moonshark prowls the final chamber of Jigow’s Emerald Grotto. It attacks creatures entering its chamber.
sections.Encounter application: If the party crossed the grotto in 10 rounds or fewer, the rivals arrive after the shark encounter. At 11 to 15 rounds, the rivals enter and roll initiative in round 3. Unless hostile to the characters, they help fight the shark. Hostile rivals pursue the amulet or interfere with the characters without intentionally killing them. At 16 rounds or more, the rivals arrive first and reduce the shark to 75 HP before the characters roll initiative. At 0 HP the shark knocks over the southern pillar, breaking open the passage to E11.
sections.Source notes: The adventure inherits the Giant Shark block and gives effects tied to a removable spear. The Huge Beast classification comes from the 2014 parent block.

name: Moorbounder
publication: Critical Role: Call of the Netherdeep
otherStatistics: Natural armor. Darkvision 60 ft. Passive Perception 11. No languages.
appearance: A sleek, broad-chested hunting cat with long ivory tusks, powerful hind legs, and large clawed paws.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast and Critical Role, Critical Role: Call of the Netherdeep, first printing, March 2022, Appendix A, Creatures, Moorbounders, p. 203. https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/cotn/creatures#Moorbounders
sections.Traits: Standing Leap. The moorbounder can long jump up to 40 ft. or high jump up to 20 ft. from a standstill or after a run.
sections.Actions: Claw. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, 5 ft. reach, one target. A hit deals 14 (4d4 + 4) slashing damage.
sections.Encounter ecology: Moorbounders hunt in the marshes and muddy foothills of Xhorhas. Experienced handlers train them for hunting and riding into battle.
sections.Encounter application: In Moorbounder Mayhem on p. 43, Justice rides a moorbounder named Rice Pudding. The mount is frightened by two bristled moorbounders and bucks as Justice hangs on.
sections.Source notes: The adventure prints a standalone Beast block on p. 203. The attack is Claw in this printing.

name: Young Horizonback Tortoise
publication: Critical Role: Call of the Netherdeep
otherStatistics: Natural armor. Passive Perception 11. Understands Goblin but cannot speak.
appearance: A fifteen-foot-tall tortoise with a high dome of overlapping shell plates, a thick beaked head, and sturdy legs.

sections.Printed source: Wizards of the Coast and Critical Role, Critical Role: Call of the Netherdeep, first printing, March 2022, Chapter 1, A Fateful Competition, J6 Herding the Horizonbacks, p. 26. Use the Ankylosaurus base block in the 2014 Monster Manual, p. 79. https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/cotn/a-fateful-competition#AdventureStart
sections.Traits: Amphibious. The tortoise can breathe air and water.
sections.Actions: Bite. Melee weapon attack, +7 to hit, 10 ft. reach, one target. A hit deals 18 (4d6 + 4) piercing damage. A creature hit must succeed on a DC 14 Strength save or fall prone.
sections.Base-block action: The inherited Ankylosaurus Tail is a +7 melee weapon attack with 10 ft. reach against one target. It deals 18 (4d6 + 4) bludgeoning damage. A creature hit must succeed on a DC 14 Strength save or fall prone.
sections.Encounter ecology: Jigow’s young horizonbacks move from a paddock to fields west of the Jumble, where they start training as mounts and mobile buildings.
sections.Encounter application: Maneuvering a tortoise takes three successful Wisdom (Animal Handling) checks, starting at DC 12 and increasing by 1 after each check. On a failed check, it bucks the rider, who must make a DC 13 Dexterity save or fall for 3 (1d6) bludgeoning damage. Remounting requires a DC 15 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check. Failure prompts a Bite. A tortoise charmed through animal friendship or a similar effect does not buck its handler on a failed check, and the handler has advantage on checks to guide it.
sections.Source notes: The printed variant gives the tortoise a Bite modeled on the 2014 Ankylosaurus Tail. The adventure describes use of Bite and never expressly removes Tail. The indexed summary presents Bite alone. The Huge Beast classification comes from the parent block.
